subject.title: [Bug]: The project won't start on Windows and WSL.

question: Should OpenClaw keep tsdown and pursue a targeted Windows/WSL wrapper or dependency fix, or should maintainers sponsor replacing the build tool for source builds?
rationale: Both paths touch the repository build and release pipeline, and the issue discussion explicitly disputes a narrow patch versus replacing tsdown; automation cannot choose that product and supply-chain direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Prove and patch narrowly
options.body: Require Windows and WSL second-build proof, then keep tsdown if a wrapper, upgrade, or upstream issue fix resolves the hang without broader build churn.

options.title: Replace tsdown
options.body: Sponsor a build-tool replacement only after maintainers accept the migration, dependency, packaging, and release-validation cost.

options.title: Defer until clearer repro
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for full logs, exact environment, and live repro before choosing any implementation direction.

recommendation.title: Prove and patch narrowly
recommendation.body: Require Windows and WSL second-build proof, then keep tsdown if a wrapper, upgrade, or upstream issue fix resolves the hang without broader build churn.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent tsdown config ownership plus broad build/tooling history makes this the clearest available decision owner.
